# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent uses 13 LUTs and 6 FFs, passes simulation, and has positive hold slack of 0.091 ns, but routed setup WNS is −0.931 ns, so timing feasibility is the first objective. The reported critical path runs from `read_ptr` through distributed RAM to `out_data[7]`; the advisor attributes much of the delay to clock insertion and pad delay. The top’s authoritative latency is 1 cycle and requires `// @latency 1`. No prior proposal outcomes are supplied.

## Hypothesis

Keeping the oldest word in a dedicated output register should remove the read-pointer-to-output-memory path and may recover setup timing, at the cost of additional FFs and next-head selection logic.

## Instruction for generator

In `sync_fifo_core`, replace the dynamically indexed `memory[read_ptr]` output path with a dedicated head register that directly drives `out_data`; update it on an accepted push into an empty FIFO and on a pop when another word remains, selecting the next word or simultaneous replacement input as required. Preserve the existing occupancy, readiness, and transfer rules, including full simultaneous pop/push, stable valid data during stalls, synchronous reset priority, and minimum accepted-transfer age of one cycle. Keep explicit pointer wrap and full-width payload behavior for every supported `WIDTH` and `DEPTH`; retain the top interface and `// @latency 1`, then judge the candidate using the fixed simulation and routed setup/hold and metric gates.
